newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Foodborne E coli disease on rise - UN health body.
newsitem.headline: Foodborne E coli disease on rise - UN health body.

text.p: The U.N. health agency reported on Wednesday an increase in foodborne infections caused by E coli bacteria leading to potentially life-threatening diseases.

A statement from the Geneva-based World Health Organisation (WHO) said there was some evidence of person-to-person spread of the infection and of transmission through contact with animals although contaminated beef was to blame in most cases.
WHO says more and more people are becoming sick from food because of changing eating habits in favour of pre-prepared food from supermarkets, takeaways and unprocessed health food.
WHO gave no statistics on most recent E coli outbreaks.
But it urged controls on meat products to avoid outbreaks like a recent one in Scotland traced to contaminated beef which it said killed 19 people out of 496 cases.
WHO food safety official Fritz Kaferstein also urged new prevention and control guidelines for ready-to-eat raw agricultural products and fresh vegetables.
Fermented sausages, yoghurt, mayonnaise and fruit juices had also been associated with recent outbreaks, he said.
The 0-157 E coli can cause bloody diarrhoea and be fatal.
